comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C29-C31, C57 regarding global genetic correlations. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical methods with nominal significance, while peer reviewers explicitly accepted findings as replicating prior work without challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C2, C32-C36 regarding local correlation findings. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate FDR correction and clear data presentation, while peer reviewers found evidence convincing and accepted HLA region concentration as reasonable.

Both address ALS-AD colocalisation (C4, C44-C46, C95-C96) with SUPPORTED evaluations. OpenEval emphasizes high correlation and posterior probability with robust sensitivity analysis (C47). Peer reviewers explicitly endorsed findings as having important implications. Strong concordance on this key result.

Partial overlap on claims C37-C38, C42-C43 regarding fine-mapping patterns. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with logical correlation between fine-mapping success and signal strength. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, noting unclear reasons why all identified regions showed positive correlations and requesting more exploration.

OpenEval addresses distinct variants (C3, C48, C53-C54) with SUPPORTED evaluation, noting low H4 probabilities and methodological limitations. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about the same pattern (C3, C48), noting majority of regions lack clear candidate variants. Disagreement on confidence level.

Both address methodological limitations in complex LD regions (C53-C56). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED while appropriately noting limitations. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning whether methodological choices adequately addressed LD complexity and requesting simulation validation.

Perfect agreement on claims C68-C72 comparing with prior work. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes well-reasoned comparison and methodological superiority of LD-based regions. Peer reviewers specifically noted improved ALS-AD evidence as a strength.

Perfect agreement on claims C73-C75 regarding interpretation of data patterns. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes reasonable interpretation with some inferential uncertainty. Peer reviewers accepted the explanatory framework without direct challenge.

Partial overlap on claims C49, C52 regarding large credible sets and LD. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate acknowledgment of limitations. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about explanations for findings differing from previous analyses, requesting demonstration via simulation.

Both address claim C56 regarding potential obstruction by LD. OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about whether true shared variants were missed. Peer reviewers also express UNCERTAINTY, questioning adequacy of methodological explanations for complex LD handling.

Perfect agreement on claims C27, C83-C84 regarding pipeline availability. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes good scientific practice for reproducibility. Peer reviewers explicitly praised the openly available pipeline as commendable and useful for diverse research fields.

Both address methodological capabilities (C1, C76-C77) with SUPPORTED evaluations. OpenEval notes demonstrated utility of well-established approaches. Peer reviewers endorsed novelty and state-of-the-art local correlation approaches, though initially requested more software justification (addressed in revision).

Perfect agreement on claims C78, C80 regarding LD reference quality control. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges known limitation while documenting appropriate validation. Peer reviewers accepted quality control procedures without raising concerns.

Partial overlap on HLA biological interpretation (C62-C64). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate citations and functional integration. Peer reviewers also SUPPORTED, noting important implications for understanding disease mechanisms. Strong concordance on biological context.

Partial overlap on biological context (C65-C67). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED through appropriate citations providing context for ALS-AD colocalisation. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted biological interpretation through overall positive assessment. Agreement on contextual claims.
